edit.description: the denial scan, widened to the second primitive beside the permission bit
the detector's gitfile fixtures and the suite's own empty gitfile set

summary: the suite's denial scan reads a wrecked worktree gitfile as a denial primitive, so a case armed that way outside a declared host reds instead of standing green over a wall win32 never raised
acceptance: the denial scan files a `gitdir:` write standing outside a host-declared case, attributes one inside such a case to it, passes over a write that is not a gitdir pointer, and reports the suite's own gitfile set empty in its own assertion
tests: the host-declaration scan reads a planted dangling gitfile as an undeclared denial
the host-declaration scan attributes a dangling gitfile to the innermost host-declared case around it
the host-declaration scan passes over a write whose content is not a gitdir pointer
pins: no case in tests/ denies by wrecking a worktree's gitfile
notes: Measured drift: five walled-wave cases armed on `writeFile(join(cwd, '.git'), 'gitdir: /flume-no-such-gitdir')` — green on posix, silently unarmed on the windows lane until 1f397af0 replaced the arming. The scan reads a permission bit alone, so a recurrence is undetectable. A source scan cannot decide the gitdir is absent, so any `gitdir:` write is the primitive; the suite holds none today, which is why the suite arm is a pin.
